stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The sheaf-theoretic closed immersion correspondence and module functors are source-defined.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals cutting out $Z$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction map
$\mathcal{F} \to i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$ induces an isomorphism
$\mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \cong i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$.
\item The functor $i^*$ is a left inverse to $i_*$, i.e., for any
$\mathcal{O}_Z$-module $\mathcal{G}$ the adjunction map
$i^*i_*\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{G}$ is an isomorphism.
\item The functor
$$
i_* :
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be the quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals cutting out $Z$.
conclusions:
For any $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ the adjunction map
$\mathcal{F} \to i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$ induces an isomorphism
$\mathcal{F}/\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} \cong i_*i^*\mathcal{F}$.

The functor $i^*$ is a left inverse to $i_*$, i.e., for any
$\mathcal{O}_Z$-module $\mathcal{G}$ the adjunction map
$i^*i_*\mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{G}$ is an isomorphism.

The functor
$$
i_* :
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F} = 0$.

reason: The closed immersion's quotient exact sequence O_X→i_*O_Z gives i_*i^*F=F/IF. The counit i^*i_*G→G is an isomorphism because the restricted structure sheaf map is surjective. Quasi-compact separated pushforward preserves quasi-coherence, and annihilation by I characterizes its fully faithful essential image.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The sheaf-theoretic closed immersion correspondence and module functors are source-defined.

The unique largest quasi-coherent G'⊂G is characterized by the Hom bijection for all quasi-coherent H.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule.
There exists a unique quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule
$\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$ with the following property:
For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{H}$ the map
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G}')
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is bijective. In particular $\mathcal{G}'$ is the largest quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ contained in $\mathcal{G}$.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}$ be a $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule.
conclusions:
There exists a unique quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule
$\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$ with the following property:
For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{H}$ the map
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G}')
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})
$$
is bijective. In particular $\mathcal{G}'$ is the largest quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-submodule of $\mathcal{F}$ contained in $\mathcal{G}$.

reason: Take the sum of all quasi-coherent submodules G_a⊂G; its image in the ambient quasi-coherent F is quasi-coherent, hence the largest such submodule. Every map from a quasi-coherent H into G has quasi-coherent image, so factors uniquely through this largest object, giving the stated Hom bijection.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The sheaf-theoretic closed immersion correspondence and module functors are source-defined.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $Z, Y \subset X$ be closed subspaces.
Let $Z \cap Y$ be the scheme theoretic intersection of $Z$ and $Y$.
Then $Z \cap Y \to Z$ and $Z \cap Y \to Y$ are closed immersions
and
$$
\xymatrix{
Z \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z \ar[d] \\
Y \ar[r] & X
}
$$
is a cartesian diagram of algebraic spaces over $S$, i.e.,
$Z \cap Y = Z \times_X Y$.
hypotheses:

Let $Z, Y \subset X$ be closed subspaces.
Let $Z \cap Y$ be the scheme theoretic intersection of $Z$ and $Y$.
conclusions:
$Z \cap Y \to Z$ and $Z \cap Y \to Y$ are closed immersions
and
$$
\xymatrix{
Z \cap Y \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z \ar[d] \\
Y \ar[r] & X
}
$$

$Z \cap Y = Z \times_X Y$.

reason: Both maps of the scheme-theoretic intersection to the original closed subspaces are closed immersions. Because scheme-theoretic intersections commute with étale localization, the cartesian square reduces to the scheme calculation.
